Annual gross revenue, year-round. Summer is priced at 81 Timberlane's own published rate ($2,036/night across 112 rate-card nights); occupancy and off-season results come from 6 comparable listings' trailing-12-month AirROI data.

Annual gross revenue. Based on trailing 12-month AirROI performance of 6 comparable properties. Occupancy is measured on open nights (nights booked ÷ nights open to guests); the comps' median is 365 open nights a year.

How occupancy is measured: the annual occupancy figures in this report are on open nights: nights booked divided by the nights the home was open to guests (AirROI excludes nights the owner blocked). Monthly and seasonal figures are AirROI's monthly occupancy. On that basis the comps booked 14% to 88% of their open nights over the last 12 months. In the summer rate-card season (Jun–Sep) they averaged 63% and from November to April 32%. In AirROI's data for this area, higher nightly rates come with lower occupancy: 22 of the 67 active lake homes in the search booked 40% or more of their open nights, and 1 of those averaged $1,000+ a night. AirROI's location estimate for a typical 4-bedroom home here is 43% occupancy at $585 a night.
How the base case is derived: This projection uses 81 Timberlane's own summer pricing and the comps' real booking patterns. Summer (Jun–Sep): the published rate card totals $228,000 for 16 weeks, or $2,036 a night. The comps booked a median 64% of nights in those months (AirROI monthly data), so 112 nights × 64% × $2,036 = $146,804. Rest of the year: the comps' median actual AirROI revenue outside those months is $44,962. Base case: $191,766, about 143 booked nights (39.2% of the year) at a blended $1,340 ADR. Conservative and Optimistic use the comps' 25th and 75th percentiles for both parts.

Cross-check: the comps' own trailing-12-month results (median revenue $184,072; AirROI's typical-home estimate $90,992) give a comp-only base of $137,532. The difference is the summer rate: the comps average well below $2,036 a night on Airbnb.

Compared with the current summer rate card: $228,000 if all 16 weeks sell. The base case assumes 64% of summer nights book at that rate, plus off-season income the property does not earn today. The base case is $36,234 below the full rate card.

Methodology

Assumptions & Methodology

Comp selection
  • 4-7 bedrooms (subject has 4; larger homes are labeled), sleeps 7-13 (subject sleeps 10, plus or minus 3), waterfront, lake access or boat slip, rated 4.8+
  • AirROI radius search within 12 miles of the subject, entire homes only
  • Must list waterfront, lake access or a boat slip in AirROI's amenity data
  • Must have AirROI trailing-12-month revenue
  • At least 3 reviews, rated 4.8+
  • At least 30 nights booked in the last 12 months (an established, active listing)
  • Mixed set: half are the highest nightly rates in the search (labeled Premium rate), half are the highest 12-month revenue (labeled Top earner)
Scenario math
  • Summer (rate-card months): published rate ÷ rate-card nights = nightly rate; × rate-card nights × the comps' AirROI occupancy in those months
  • Off-season: the comps' actual AirROI revenue and booked nights in all other months
  • Conservative / Base / Optimistic: 25th percentile / median / 75th percentile of the comps for both parts; total = summer + off-season
  • Occupancy = booked nights ÷ 365; ADR = revenue ÷ booked nights
Data sources
  • AirROI /listings/search/radius, /listings/metrics/all and /calculator/estimate: comp revenue, occupancy, ADR, availability, monthly performance and AirROI's location estimate
  • Published rate card: Published 2027 weekly rates, Yankee Pedlar (winnire.com)
  • Raw AirROI responses are saved alongside this report
